subject: DPA negotiation: deployment-specific routing, subprocessors & e-sign options (FinSecure)
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finsecure.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@finsecure.com
Date: 2027-08-11T09:12:00Z
Subject: DPA: deployment-specific data routing & subprocessors

Connor / Lauren —

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our procurement diligence for the Redwood platform we need a DPA that explicitly accounts for differences between (a) Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPUs in our EU region) and (b) Private/VPC/on-prem deployments where we manage networking and key material. Our immediate asks: 

- Can you provide a redline that separates obligations by deployment mode (Dedicated vs Private) rather than a single flat annex? In particular we need explicit commitments on: data routing, cross-border transfer restrictions, and subprocessors per mode.
- A current subprocessor matrix by deployment mode (who will process customer data for Dedicated vs Private).
- Confirmation of the transfer mechanism for EU data (SCCs + DPA text, or another mechanism) and whether Redwood will sign SCCs as the data processor.
- Clarify KMS/HSM options and whether Redwood will support customer-managed keys for Private deployments.
- SOC 2 Type II report and audit contact.

I've attached a short list of questions (FinSecure_DPA_Qs.xlsx) to guide redlines. We prefer AdobeSign for execution, but DocuSign also fine. Please let us know a timeline — procurement is hoping to execute within two weeks.

Regards,
Oliver
Head of IT Risk, FinSecure
Attachment: FinSecure_DPA_Qs.xlsx (Spreadsheet)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finsecure.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-12T13:45:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA: deployment-specific data routing & subprocessors

Oliver —

Thanks for the clear list. I've started a redline that explicitly sections obligations by deployment mode and attached an initial draft (Redline_DPA_Connor_v1.docx). High-level notes:

- Dedicated (EU region): We can commit to region pinning in the contract and operationally route EU-customer traffic to our EU tenant and EU-hosted GPU cluster. For transfers we propose SCCs + an updated DPA exhibit that names the EU host region and subprocessors used for that region.
- Private / VPC / On-prem: By design customer-managed networking and optional on-prem packages mean no cross-border processing is performed by Redwood if the customer chooses on-prem. For VPC-Hosted Private, we propose language that: (a) allows the customer to require customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) and (b) limits Redwood subprocessors to support/maintenance services only and explicitly lists them in Exhibit A.

Open items we still need from you: the specific AdobeSign vs DocuSign preference, and whether FinSecure requires Redwood to sign the SCCs as processor or if FinSecure will be the data controller to adopt processor-to-processor clauses.

I've linked our working subprocessor matrix in the draft. We'll follow up with SOC 2 evidence in a private drive link.

Next steps proposed: 1) quick 30-min call to align on KMS and transfer mechanism, 2) I push a redline iteration after that and include Lauren for legal language. Are you available Tuesday (Aug 14) or Wednesday (Aug 15)?

Thanks —
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redline_DPA_Connor_v1.docx (Word document)
From: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@finsecure.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finsecure.com>, legal@finsecure.com
Date: 2027-08-13T08:07:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA: deployment-specific data routing & subprocessors

Connor —

Thanks for the draft. A few points from legal:

- We need the DPA to identify the lawful basis for processing and the specific transfer safeguard. FinSecure's preference is that for Dedicated EU-hosted workloads Redwood executes the SCCs as processor. If Redwood cannot sign the controller-processor SCCs, we will need processor-to-processor addenda and a documented technical guarantee that no EU personal data leaves the EU.
- For Private/on-prem, our requirement is 'no cross-border processing' unless we explicitly opt-in. Please add a clear opt-in flow in the exhibit.
- Please confirm whether Redwood will allow customer-managed KMS for VPC/Private and provide a short list of any limitations.

We are attaching our initial legal comments (FinSecure_comments_v1.pdf). We prefer AdobeSign for this agreement — we are generally faster on that platform.

Patricia Gomez
Senior Counsel, FinSecure
Attachment: FinSecure_comments_v1.pdf (PDF)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@finsecure.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finsecure.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-14T10:31:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA: deployment-specific data routing & subprocessors

Patricia / Oliver —

Appreciate the detailed feedback. A few clarifications and proposed changes from our side: 

1) Exhibit A — Subprocessors by deployment mode: we'll provide a CSV that lists subprocessors and the modes they apply to (Hosted/Hosted-EU-only, Dedicated, Private/VPC, On-prem support). See attached ExhibitA_subprocessors.csv.

2) SCCs & transfer mechanism: Redwood can execute the standard European Commission SCCs for processor-controller relationships where applicable. For Dedicated EU region customers we will sign the SCCs as processor and operationally isolate EU workloads. For Private/on-prem where the customer manages infrastructure, the DPA will include an opt-in checkbox and the exhibit will document that no cross-border transfers are performed unless explicitly accepted.

3) KMS: Customer-managed KMS is available for Private/VPC deployments. Limitations: (a) for full on-prem deployments where the customer runs runtime entirely within their network, Redwood does not hold encryption keys; (b) for VPC-hosted private deployments we offer BYOK with HSM-backed keys but require key provisioning procedures and a short validation window. We will add the KMS operational checklist as an annex.

4) Audit rights & SOC2: We'll provide SOC 2 Type II on a secured link and are open to scheduled audit windows for in-scope Dedicated components. Please specify the scope for the audit request (e.g., hosting network, access controls).

I will prepare a new redline with these points and propose concrete language for the opt-in path and Exhibit A.

Lauren Bishop
Legal Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: ExhibitA_subprocessors.csv (CSV)
